layer: L6 / package-private current Graph-native evaluation authority
question: How should the TypeScript eval replace the D-number compatibility stack with one current Graph-native authority that can truthfully classify admitted failures, provide bounded corrective feedback and validate public behavior without hidden-verifier leakage?
decision: The TypeScript package adds one package-private current Graph-native eval authority. Caller-owned executors may perform asynchronous materialization, provider, tool, public-semantic-validation, hidden-verifier and cleanup effects, but may return only bounded immutable results; only exact provenance-bound facts admitted by the Graph may affect findings, corrective feedback, budget, stopping, cleanup or canonical persistence. Executor, tool-rejection, public-semantic-validation and hidden-verifier failures remain distinct fact families. A zero-side-effect exact-replacement-not-applicable rejection may cause at most one Graph-authored reinspection-and-fresh-mutation correction per run, only after the exact failed effect result and rejection fact are admitted and only when the Graph has reserved the entire remaining correction path; replay, state drift, a second rejection or insufficient headroom causes arm-local cleanup. Public semantic validation uses independent actor-visible behavioral scenarios derived from public acceptance criteria and never hidden verifier material, an expected patch or source-substring matching. The current finding projection emits public-semantic-validation-failed only from an admitted failed public-semantic result and hidden-verifier-failed only from an admitted failed hidden-verifier result. New current artifacts are Graph-derived only and generate no legacy observation, scorecard or generation. graphrefly:D691 through graphrefly:D782 artifacts remain immutable audit evidence and are not current runtime dependencies. The first implementation is package-private and injected no-network only, with exact six-arm serial execution, cold-independent warm arms, replay/state/headroom/second-failure rejection, cleanup, privacy, provenance, canonical replay and failure-atomic persistence QA. causalAttribution=undetermined and efficacyClaim=none are fixed. This decision changes no library behavior, public API, export, protocol or conformance and authorizes no credential read, claim, network/provider, charged call or automatic rerun.
rationale: The consumed graphrefly:D782 evidence proves that sanitized exact-replacement rejection facts were persisted but immediately followed by cleanup, so the model never received the admitted failure needed to correct its mutation. It also proves that public semantic failures were derived from brittle source-substring checks and were mislabeled as hidden-verifier failures even though the hidden verifier never ran. Continuing to layer historical D-number adapters would preserve duplicated authorities and compatibility coupling. A single current Graph-owned correction and evidence path keeps async execution outside the synchronous graph while making every decision and durable claim derivable from exact admitted facts, which is the intended GraphReFly use in the eval.

completion.complete_when: The package-private current eval completes injected no-network six-arm qualification with exact Graph-derived failure classification, bounded replacement-rejection recovery, independent public behavioral validation, canonical replay and failure-atomic private persistence, and all TypeScript and federated-authority gates are green.
completion.historical_when: A later graphrefly-ts decision explicitly supersedes this current eval authority or the package-private evaluation program is retired.

layer: L6 / package-private current Graph-native real-provider pre-live architecture
question: How should the D1 current Graph-native eval acquire a provider-capable pre-live boundary without creating an adapter evidence ledger or moving retry, budget and stopping decisions outside the Graph?
decision: Using TypeScript commit fa6a731695c63a9da6681e76c07bd1ed3182e7a2, the D1 bundle artifact sha256:1ef86a1aede3ba96614b0fe9d39ac3c14c630d37f27fd878982991afcf3937ae and the D1 implementation manifest sha256:6a9151b68dcdcb983d818ec0af9eb3ec6819883ec78a883b012edeae6229bc6d as the exact baseline, the TypeScript package adds a new package-private current Graph-native real-provider pre-live architecture. Graph-authored route and task envelopes, bounded runtime tool-argument facts, provider usage, cost and retry reconciliation, and a material-free canonical projection are the sole authority for provider-capable evaluation decisions and evidence. The adapter executes exactly one admitted asynchronous effect per invocation, returns one bounded immutable result fact, maintains no evidence ledger, and never decides retry, next arm or stopping. Material-bearing task and tool arguments remain bounded ephemeral Graph runtime facts; durable canonical evidence contains only Graph-derived material-free coordinates and digests. The first D2 implementation must complete exact six-arm injected no-network qualification covering retry, failure, cleanup, privacy, provenance, failure-atomic persistence and implementation drift. D1 source and artifacts remain immutable qualification inputs. This decision changes no library behavior, public API, export, protocol or conformance and authorizes no credential read, dispatch claim, control-plane or provider network call, charged call or automatic rerun; a live numeric approval may be considered only after D2 qualification is frozen.
rationale: D1 established one Graph authority for effect admission, correction and durable evidence, but its provider effect result intentionally exposes only tool references and aggregate cost/elapsed values. A real-provider boundary additionally needs a Graph-authored model-visible envelope, bounded tool arguments and exact usage/retry reconciliation. Placing those concerns in an adapter-side loop or side ledger would recreate the imperative coordinator and duplicate evidence authority that D1 removed. A versioned D2 runtime keeps asynchronous I/O in caller-owned adapters while making every model request, retry decision, tool argument and persistent claim traceable to Graph admission.

completion.complete_when: The D2 package-private provider-capable architecture completes an exact six-arm injected no-network qualification whose Graph-authored route/task envelopes, bounded runtime tool arguments, provider usage/cost/retry reconciliations and material-free canonical projection pass failure, cleanup, privacy, provenance, atomic-persistence, implementation-drift and federated-authority gates without credential, claim or network access.
completion.historical_when: A later graphrefly-ts decision explicitly supersedes the D2 provider-capable pre-live architecture or the current package-private evaluation program is retired.

layer: L6 / package-private current Graph-native inspection-batch admission
question: How should the current Graph-native eval handle a provider response containing several independent read-only inspection intents without misclassifying it as executor failure or moving orchestration into the adapter?
decision: Using the consumed graphrefly-ts:D4 canonical Graph evidence as the immutable failure baseline, the TypeScript eval adds a new package-private D5 Graph authority in which an initial provider response may contain a bounded non-empty batch of read-file intents. The Graph preserves the exact provider order and independently admits and executes each read-file as one serial tool effect; only after every admitted inspection result is reconciled may the Graph advance to the mutation phase. The adapter remains one-effect-at-a-time and may not split, reorder, loop over or execute the batch, maintain an evidence ledger, or decide the next effect. Any non-read inspection intent, duplicate/replayed admission, state drift, budget/headroom exhaustion, tool failure or oversized batch fails closed with Graph-authored findings and cleanup. D1 through D4 artifacts and source closures remain immutable audit evidence and are not runtime dependencies of D5. D5 first completes a six-arm injected no-network qualification using the exact four-read pattern observed in D4, with per-read admission/reconciliation bijection, seriality, bounds, failure, cleanup, privacy, provenance, canonical replay, atomic persistence and implementation-drift QA. causalAttribution=undetermined and efficacyClaim=none remain fixed. This decision changes no library behavior, public API, protocol or conformance and authorizes no credential read, claim, network/provider call, charged call or automatic rerun.
rationale: D4 proved that the live provider consistently returned four valid read-file intents in each arm while the existing authority accepted exactly one, causing all six arms to stop before any tool effect and to be mislabeled executor-failed. Serial Graph admission of the original bounded batch preserves provider order and Graph-only authority while avoiding both adapter-side orchestration and a second evidence source.

completion.complete_when: The D5 package-private authority completes a no-network six-arm qualification proving exact ordered admission and reconciliation of the D4 four-read batch, subsequent mutation/validation progress, fail-closed negative paths, cleanup, privacy, provenance, canonical replay, atomic persistence and implementation drift without credential, claim or network access.
completion.historical_when: A later graphrefly-ts decision explicitly supersedes D5 or the package-private evaluation program is retired.
